question: On 12 open research questions, does the AIL+MoIE five-stage procedure (C4) produce hypotheses rated more novel by a blind judge than compute-matched best-of-n versions of few-shot (C1-bon), chain-of-thought (C2-bon) and tree-of-thoughts (C3-bon) prompting, using the same model and the same total token budget?
hypothesis: H1c: the AIL+MoIE procedure rates more novel than each compute-matched best-of-n baseline. This is the primary hypothesis of the Hermes12 pre-registration, re-instantiated in a new instrument; the original Hermes12 package (local to the owner's machine) is a different instrument.
matching: Per question, budget B is the mean total tokens (input plus output) of C4 over its repetitions. For each baseline, n is the largest integer such that n single passes plus one selector call fit within B; the selector call is charged to the baseline. The report states the achieved cost ratio.

judges.description: a model of a different family from the generator
a second judge: a human rater or a second model of a different family

primary.test: one-sided paired sign-flip permutation across questions; Hedges g from per-question differences

falsification: H1c is NOT supported if any of the three contrasts has Holm-adjusted p of 0.05 or more, or Hedges g of 0.5 or less. If judge agreement (Krippendorff alpha for novelty) is below 0.4, the result is inconclusive, not supported. A tie is not supported. Inherited from the Hermes12 pre-registration: if H1c fails across two independent replications the integration claim is reported as false; the lab decides whether this run counts as one of the two.
limits: The standard is a rubric applied by a model judge. It is weaker than an executable check and measures what a judge rates as novel, which is not the same as what is novel or true.

If a judge is the same model or family as the generator, self-preference bias can inflate ratings; the analysis flags a judge that used the same adapter, and the registered requirement is a different family.
12 author-written questions and 2 repetitions per question is a small sample. With 12 questions the registered rule has limited power to detect a modest effect (see controls.json).
C5 (the retrieval-backed MoIE arm) and hypotheses H2 and H3 of the original package are not tested here; coherence non-inferiority is reported as a secondary check only.
The Positive Deviant Scout uses the model's own knowledge, so cited anomalies are not verified and may be invented; the scout prompt asks the model not to invent cases.
One generator model is tested. A result says nothing about other models.
Blinding hides arm labels but not writing style; a judge may be able to guess which arm produced a text.

The generator's context window must be large enough that MoIE's accumulated stage context is not truncated; the Ollama adapter is run with OLLAMA_NUM_CTX=8192 and fails closed if a prompt fills the window.
stopping_rule: One revision pass to prompts and questions after the controls pass, then lock. No edits after lock; a change means a new experiment directory.
